sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang begins at row J, with the top part of the stage cut off from around row M.
sn.sh: Mezzanine overhang begins at row J

sn.c: Views of the side of the stage become gradually more restricted the further out you sit, with far side aisle seats most affected.
sn.sh: Far side aisle seats most affected

sn.c: The Balcony overhang is more obvious in the back half.
sn.sh: Balcony overhang in the back half

sn.c: A seat in row A of the Balcony is perfect for combining extra legroom, the best view, and good value for money.
sn.sh: Extra legroom and the best view in row A

sn.c: Row A of the Center Mezzanine has a great general overview of the stage.

vs.sum: The St. James Theatre offers good sightlines for most seats, though the lack of a solid rake can be an issue if someone tall sits in front of you. The sound quality is generally good, but the tight legroom can be uncomfortable for taller patrons. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic and grand interior, while facilities are average with standard amenities.

acc.note: No steps from sidewalk to Orchestra. No elevator. Mezzanine up 29 steps, Balcony up 76 steps.
